title: Non-Hermitian topology in driven-dissipative systems: correspondence with quantum correlations and a resource for entanglement
abstract: Directional amplification, in which signals are amplified selectively depending on their propagation direction, is a key resource for quantum information processing and stands in one-to-one correspondence with non-trivial non-Hermitian topology. So far, this correspondence has concerned the mean fields, and thus classical response. Here we turn to the quantum fluctuations, giving access to correlations and entanglement. For phase-preserving amplifiers, we derive analytic expressions for the normal and anomalous correlations, showing that non-trivial topology produces correlations that grow exponentially with the distance between modes and approach the largest values compatible with the uncertainty relations. The associated correlation length diverges at the topological phase transition. Entanglement nonetheless remains local, set by the competition between normalised anomalous correlations and the asymmetry of the mode occupations. For the bosonic Kitaev chain, a phase-sensitive amplifier, the system instead splits into two halves that are internally fully correlated yet mutually uncorrelated. Our work prepares the ground for exploring the quantum properties of non-Hermitian topological systems with state-of-the-art platforms such as cavity optomechanics and superconducting circuits.
summary: This paper establishes a quantum generalization of the connection between non-Hermitian topology and directional amplification. It shows that non-trivial topology generates long-range quantum correlations in driven-dissipative systems, while entanglement remains localized. This provides a powerful theoretical tool for designing quantum devices based on topological principles.
main_problem: The paper extends the understanding of non-Hermitian topology from classical mean-field responses to the quantum realm by analyzing quantum fluctuations, correlations, and entanglement in driven-dissipative systems.
main_result: Non-trivial non-Hermitian topology leads to exponentially growing, long-range quantum correlations, while entanglement remains local, governed by the competition between these correlations and mode occupation asymmetry.
method: The authors utilize quantum Langevin equations, analyzing second moments to calculate normal and anomalous correlations, and employing the winding number to characterize the non-Hermitian topology.
model_or_system: The study focuses on driven-dissipative bosonic chains, exemplified by phase-preserving amplifiers and the bosonic Kitaev chain. The dynamics are governed by a non-Hermitian dynamic matrix H.

important_parameters: Cooperativity ($C$), system size ($N$), and the topological phase transition point.
main_assumptions: The analysis often assumes a directional, cascaded evolution structure for the correlation analysis, and the initial correspondence was limited to mean fields.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate directional topological amplifiers, the dependence of correlations on distance (showing divergence at phase transitions), and the evolution of entanglement at system boundaries.
paper_structure: The work progresses from establishing the classical mean-field correspondence to deriving analytic expressions for quantum correlations, analyzing the divergence of the correlation length, and finally detailing the local nature of entanglement in specific models like the Kitaev chain.
why_interesting: This work provides a deep theoretical link between topological invariants (non-Hermitian geometry) and measurable quantum resources (correlations/entanglement) in open quantum systems, directly applicable to cavity optomechanics and superconducting circuits.
